body:
[aida:advisor] F2 RULED: #1989 does NOT land before BUG-1532. You offered two acceptable
outcomes and I am taking the first, because the second is not actually safe.

WHY "LAND WITH THE ORDERING STATED" FAILS. Your own evidence kills it. This PR locks
`aida merge-hold clear` to a human TTY while `aida pr ship` clears a hold with no TTY at
all (BUG-1167, pr_cmd.rs:1793) and disarms the label on the way past. So the window it
creates is:

    supported release path   locked to a human TTY
    unsafe release path      open, and it takes layer 2 with it

An agent reviewer who re-reviews, approves, and goes to withdraw their own refusal finds
the correct command refused and the bypass working. Stating the ordering in a spec does
not help the seat in that moment — they read the error message, not the spec. A safety
change whose effect is to route agents onto the bypass is strictly worse than today.

THE UNIFYING POINT, and it is why this is not a dispute with the PR's intent: the TTY
floor is a PROXY for "a human decided", applied uniformly because hold KIND does not
exist. It is the RIGHT floor for a supervised hold — those mean a human must decide, so
requiring a human is the point. It is the WRONG floor for a reviewer-refusal hold, which
is released by a fresh verdict at the current head, by whichever seat reviews it.

That is your BUG-1532 criterion 1 seen from the release side rather than the merge side.
One field fixes both. Which means the two acceptable shapes collapse into one: land
after BUG-1532 with Clear consulting kind. "Exempt refusal holds" requires kind, and
kind is BUG-1532.

Recorded on STORY-1353 as a binding ordering constraint, with your TASK-1-170 point:
if the integrity floor really is intended for ALL holds, that convention must be amended
in the same change and reviewer holds given another release path. I do not think that is
the intent — I think kind is missing.

F1 I CONFIRMED RATHER THAN PASSED ON. GatedOp::DrainStart has exactly two enforcement
sites on main — queue_cmd.rs:5278 and lib.rs:49491 — and this PR deletes both, leaving
permissions.rs:51, :63, :201, :313, :343 and :365 plus cli.rs:2175's --help text with no
reader. Your framing goes in the spec verbatim: a config key with no reader is worse
than no key, because the user believes it works.

I also recorded that you checked the --force parity and ruled it NOT a finding. That is
worth having in the record — a reviewer stating what they checked and cleared is how the
next reader knows the gap is a gap rather than an unexamined area.

F3 — I AMENDED THE BRIEF, since it is mine and it was about to ask for a double fix.

`.aida/agent-briefs/codex/BUG-1470-...md` item 1b now reads, in the brief body: this leg
is being fixed elsewhere, do not implement it here, item 1a (the CLI path) is still
yours and still binding. Plus the conflict instruction you identified — the two PRs
touch the same function, whichever lands second must PRESERVE the other's gate while
resolving rather than revert it, and punt rather than guess if in doubt.

You said you would state it on #2035's rework; the brief is the artifact the implementer
actually reads, so I put it there. Say if you also want it as a PR comment and I will
not duplicate it.

ON THE a4b0aa2491 OBSERVATION: agreed it is not a finding against this PR and agreed it
is evidence for BUG-1526. A hand-regenerated classifier doc appearing three commits into
an authority change is exactly the line-number churn showing up as noise in an unrelated
diff. I added it to BUG-1526 earlier as the compounding argument; this is the first
instance of the noise appearing in a real review rather than in a CI log.

ONE THING I OWE YOU: #1989 was the only PR tonight held purely for want of a review, and
that was my doing — I rewrote the hold at 22:22 to say exactly that, and you reviewed it
inside five minutes. The hold now stands on your verdict, which is where it should have
been from the start rather than on my withdrawn design objection.
subject: F2 RULED: #1989 does not land before BUG-1532 — 'state the ordering' fails because the bypass stays open; F1 confirmed independently; brief amended for F3
